correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed on arbitrary measurable spaces: both coordinate projections bound individual TV by the heterogeneous distance; the labelled lift has four disjoint cells of mass 1/4, giving an exact 1/4+1/2+1/4 TV decomposition; tensor telescoping gives each diagonal distance at most twice the corresponding marginal distance; forgetting labels is TV-contractive. Consequently homogenized TV <= 3/2 heterogeneous TV. For the explicit three-atom family, the signed square-mass matrix has exactly three positive entries, summing to epsilon(3-epsilon)/2 while original TV=epsilon, proving asymptotic sharpness. Exact rational test code only corroborates finite cases and is not used as an infinite proof.

residual_risks: Although highly relevant primary full text and semantic/public literature were searched, an unindexed exact n=2 equivalent could predate this result; no independent priority certification has been performed.

value.rationale: The precise optimal finite-coordinate coefficient is an explicitly motivated instance of the open general-alphabet homogenization-constant question. It distinguishes categorical from Bernoulli worst cases and supplies a natural three-atom extremal mechanism, thereby deciding the full n=2 model on arbitrary spaces. This is not merely recalculation of a known table or an arbitrary slice: two coordinates are the first setting where the homogenization map can amplify TV, and the constant has an exact operational interpretation as worst-case statistical distinguishability inflation. No claim of a general n theorem is needed.
